methods.name: GERALDINE (Google Earth Engine supRaglAciaL Debris INput dEtector)
methods.summary: GERALDINE is a tool built on Google Earth Engine that processes Landsat imagery to identify new supraglacial debris additions. It uses cloud masking, NDSI thresholding to distinguish debris from ice, and a pixel-based reducer to compare maximum debris extent between a user-defined time period and the preceding year.
methods.verbatim: GERALDINE code and the validation dataset are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3524414 (Smith et al., 2020).

code_links.name: GERALDINE code
code_links.summary: The GERALDINE code, along with a usage guide, made available via a specific Zenodo record for reproducing the study's results.

availability.author_statement: Full availability statement, with shared links.

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory and other input datasets are referenced and publicly accessible via USGS, RGI Consortium, and IRIS DMC. The custom GERALDINE code and validation dataset are provided via a persistent Zenodo link.
